newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks fade at close to end weaker.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks fade at close to end weaker.

text.p: The Australian stock market fell away at the close on Tuesday to end the day near its lows after opening firmer in line with a stronger Wall St.
The All Ordinaries Index ended at 2,650.5, down 16.7 points after a 44 point fall on Monday.
Share price index futures eased eight points, narrowing its discount to the physical index from 12.2 to 2.5 points.
"There was a bit of arbitrage activity and a couple of sell portfolios, which dragged the majors down," said a Sydney-based fund manager.
The late sell-off hit most major stocks, particularly the banks, although the gold sector provided a bright spot by holding its stronger tone.
"We just ran out of puff," said a Sydney broker. "Maybe there's a bit of nervousness about the rest of the week in the U.S.," he added.
The bank sector lost almost 1.5 percent as the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group shed 23 cents to A$9.96 and the Commonwealth Bank fell 28 cents to A$16.37.
Shares in BHP closed a cent firmer at A$17.02 after recent heavy falls due to management changes, but the market bellwether ended off its high of the day of A$17.28.
Hoyts Cinemas topped turnover after SBC Warburg crossed 11.6 million shares, or 4.7 percent of its capital, at A$2.65 a share.

Brokers were unsure of the identity of the buyer or seller, but noted that property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp last week sold eight million Hoyts shares, reducing its stake to about five percent from 9.6 percent previously.
Brokers said the market was awaiting results from Commonwealth Bank and miner WMC Ltd, both due on Wednesday.
The Commonwealth is expected to post a six percent annual net profit rise to A$1.19 billion, while WMC is seen plunging 44 percent to A$218 million on the back of weak metals prices.

In the local bond market, the 10-year Australian bond yield ended down one basis point at 6.82 percent, while the Australian dollar failed to break US0.7400, but held overnight gains in late afternoon trade at $0.7389/94.
